# Research note per phase

Every phase PR (Phase 0..11) lands a research note under `docs/research/phase-<N>-<topic>.md`. This is the per-PR evidence trail the parent plan Â§6.4 mandates. The pattern is set by [`phase-0-github-setup.md`](../../docs/research/phase-0-github-setup.md), [`phase-0-system-requirements.md`](../../docs/research/phase-0-system-requirements.md), [`phase-0-issues-execution.md`](../../docs/research/phase-0-issues-execution.md), and [`phase-1-scaffold-execution.md`](../../docs/research/phase-1-scaffold-execution.md).

## Required sections

```markdown
# Phase N - <topic> (research note)

> Research note backing the <PR id> PR.
> Parent plan: ...
> Sub-plan: ...

## Scope
## Sources (retrieved YYYY-MM-DD)
## Decisions
## Open follow-ups
## Implementation Reference

- PR: *to be filled at merge*
- Merged on: *to be filled at merge*
```

## Source freshness rule

Every cited source must have a retrieval date in its citation block. The retrieval date must be **at most 14 days old at PR open time** for any source that may change between releases (vendor docs, GitHub READMEs, web articles). Standards documents (IEC, ECSS, NPR, DO, IACS, ASAM, ISO) are exempt from the 14-day rule but must cite the edition/revision.

## When the rule fires

- Any PR with a parent-plan `phase/*` label.
- Any PR that introduces a new file under `docs/adr/` or `docs/research/`.

## When the rule does NOT fire

- Pure status-sync PRs (e.g. PR #6) that only flip todo flags - they ride on the prior PR's research note.
- Trivial refactor PRs that don't change behaviour and don't touch traced code.

## CI enforcement (lands in PR-4)

`pr-title.yml` checks PR labels: if `phase/*` is set, the diff must include a new or modified file under `docs/research/`. Failure blocks merge.
